title: Worked Examples — Only Where One Earns Its Slide
description: A worked example is not a ritual. It earns a slide where the learner could follow every word and still not be able to DO the thing — a procedure, algorithm, calculation, address or state translation, traced sequence, or numeric trade-off. It must be OMITTED for definitional, classificatory and terminological topics: 'what a file is' needs a definition and a mental model, not an invented trace. The deterministic half checks the share cap (worked examples <= 30% of slides); the LLM half judges whether each example was warranted and whether a topic that needed one went without.
criterion: Every working_example slide is on a topic the learner must be able to EXECUTE, and traces it step by step. No example manufactured for a definitional topic. Conversely, no procedural/computational takeaway left with prose only. Worked examples are at most 30% of the slides.

rubric.5: Examples exactly where they are needed, each traced step by step; none manufactured.
rubric.3: One borderline example, or one procedural topic that would have benefited from a trace.
rubric.1: An example invented for a definitional topic, a procedural topic left with no trace, or the deck dominated by examples.
